sections.overview: A rare desert dunnart known from scattered sites in Australia.
sections.identification: Its tail is pale above, dark below and tipped with a crest of stiff black hairs.
sections.habitat: It favours structurally dense spinifex hummocks and long-unburned sand plains or dune slopes.
sections.diet: Its diet includes many ants; a comparative study also found ants important for the hairy-footed dunnart, Sminthopsis hirtipes.
sections.behavior: It forages mainly from dusk to dawn.
sections.reproduction: Wild breeding usually follows winter rains and can be delayed when food is scarce.
sections.ecology: Wildfire can destroy dense cover and shelter sites it needs.
sections.conservation: It is Endangered under Australian federal law and Vulnerable on the global IUCN Red List.
